empires.name: The Middle Kingdom
empires.note: Numbers you cannot count, and crossbows issued in ranks. Their walled cities are the largest anywhere - a siege becomes a second city camped outside the gate, and they can wait longer than you.

places.name: Chang'an
places.note: The throne. A hundred walled wards inside one great wall; the gates shut at the drum and do not open for you.

places.name: Luoyang
places.note: The eastern capital, burned and rebuilt so often the masons keep a permanent camp outside it.

places.name: Yangzhou
places.note: Where the canal meets the river - salt and grain stacked in sheds, guards who count barges instead of men.

places.name: Guangzhou
places.note: Southern port thick with foreign silver, and three months of marching from any relief column.

places.name: Chengdu
places.note: Rice and brocade behind the gorges; one road in, and a hundred men can hold it.

places.name: Dunhuang
places.note: Last water before the sand. Caravans pay the garrison, and the garrison pays nobody.

places.name: Bianzhou
places.note: Grown fat on canal transhipment - the wall went up in a hurry and it shows.

places.name: Jiangling
places.note: Middle river landing where the winter barges tie up three deep under the bank.

places.name: Taiyuan
places.note: Guards the northern road. Horse pasture, and men raised expecting raiders.

empires.name: The Shogunate of Japan
empires.note: Few, but every one of them trained from childhood. A samurai will accept your duel and win it; the ones you never see come over the wall at night and leave before the alarm.

places.name: Heian-kyo
places.note: The throne. Wide streets and no city wall - the mountains are the wall, and every pass into them is held.

places.name: Kamakura
places.note: The warrior capital, sunk in a bowl of hills; seven narrow cuts are the only ways in.

places.name: Sakai
places.note: Free merchant port. It pays for its own ditch, its own wall, and its own spearmen.

places.name: Hakata
places.note: The landing beach on the strait, with a stone wall built along it for exactly this.

places.name: Nara
places.note: Old capital of temples, and armed monks who answer to no lord at all.

places.name: Hiraizumi
places.note: Northern gold paid for the halls here; the roads to them are long, thin and cold.

places.name: Kagoshima
places.note: A bay under a smoking mountain. The clan here fights first and reports afterwards.

places.name: Tosa
places.note: Rough southern coast of whalers and swordsmen, with no road worth the name.

places.name: Ise
places.note: Shrine town, pilgrims all year, and nothing worth taking but the offerings.
